purpose: Relugolix is used to treat advanced prostate cancer in men by lowering testosterone levels, which helps slow cancer growth. It is also used in women (combined with estradiol and norethindrone) to manage heavy menstrual bleeding caused by uterine fibroids or pain from endometriosis. It comes as a pill you take by mouth once a day.
how_it_works: Your body normally makes a hormone called GnRH that tells your body to produce sex hormones like testosterone or estrogen. Relugolix blocks the GnRH receptor, which quickly signals your body to stop making those hormones. In prostate cancer, lowering testosterone helps starve the cancer cells so they cannot grow as fast.
common_side_effects: Hot flashes or hot flushes, fatigue or feeling tired, low sex drive, erectile problems in men, joint or muscle aches, weight gain, increased blood sugar or cholesterol levels, and mood changes such as feeling sad or irritable.
warnings: Relugolix can increase the risk of heart problems such as heart attack or stroke, especially in men with existing heart disease — talk to your doctor right away if you have chest pain, shortness of breath, or sudden weakness. It can weaken your bones over time, raising the risk of fractures. Do not stop taking it suddenly without talking to your doctor first. Tell your doctor about all other medications you take, especially heart rhythm drugs, because serious drug interactions can occur. Women using Myfembree should not use it if they are pregnant, as it can harm an unborn baby.
typical_dosing: For prostate cancer (Orgovyx): The starting dose is 360 mg (three 120 mg tablets) taken by mouth on the first day, then 120 mg once daily every day after that. For uterine fibroids or endometriosis (Myfembree): One combination tablet is taken by mouth once daily. Always take it at the same time each day, with or without food.
